messages.content: Implement a Python function from a JSON behavioral card. The card is the only task specification. Return a JSON object with a single string field code containing executable Python source. Define solve with the card's exact signature. Use only Python's standard library. Allowed imports: math, itertools, functools, collections, heapq, bisect, statistics, fractions, operator, typing. Do not import or call NumPy, SymPy, NetworkX or any other third-party library. Do not read files, use network, introspection, eval, exec, input or print. Implement computations yourself using built-ins and the allowed standard library. Return plain JSON-compatible values, not iterators or sets; use string keys in dictionaries. Include any helper functions in the code. No tests or main block. Raise ValueError where the card requires it.

Implement this card:
{
  "algorithm": [
    "Start from n-1 and decrement by 1 until a prime number is found",
    "Use the property that potential primes are located at 6*j +/- 1 to optimize the search",
    "Check divisibility by integers up to the square root of the candidate number",
    "Return the first prime number encountered during the search"
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "n must be an integer between 3 and 5000 inclusive",
    "The output must be a plain Python integer with no symbolic objects",
    "The search must be optimized using the 6j +/- 1 pattern to reduce unnecessary checks",
    "The algorithm must terminate within a reasonable time for n up to 5000"
  ],
  "edge_cases": [
    "When n is 3, return 2",
    "When n is 4, return 3",
    "When n is 5, return 3",
    "When n is 6, return 5"
  ],
  "inputs": "An integer n where 3 <= n <= 5000",
  "method_id": "sympy.prevprime",
  "output": "A plain Python integer representing the largest prime number less than n",
  "purpose": "Return the largest prime number strictly less than the input integer n",
  "signature": "solve(n)"
}
